_doc: How the mayor talks someone round (Systems/Negotiation.cs): swaying a councillor before a vote, talking down a guild's demand or strike, bringing a holding-out ally to march. The player chooses the approach. Each is the mayor's d20 + skill against the other side's passive Insight (10 + their bonus) or, for a threat, their Wisdom save bonus + 10, plus dc. win is what their regard (a councillor's loyalty, a guild's standing, an ally's standing) moves on a success, crit more on a natural 20, lose on a failure, and loseMandate the Mandate a failure costs (a lie found out). A councillor or (later) a notable trained in the skill, and loyal enough (help), lends a hand: advantage.

approaches.name: Persuade
approaches.text: Reason and goodwill. Costs little if it fails.

approaches.name: Intimidate
approaches.text: A hard word. Works more often, but they resent it even when it does.

approaches.name: Deceive
approaches.text: A clever lie. Easiest of all, and ruinous if they see through it.

sway.text: {approach}: the mayor takes {name} aside before the vote ({roll}). {result}
sway.lost: The {seat} keeps their vote, and remembers being asked.

guild.won: {approach}: the mayor sits down with {master} of the {name} ({roll}), and {want}.
guild.lost: {approach}: the mayor sits down with {master} of the {name} ({roll}). The guild will not budge, and thinks less of the town hall for asking.

ally.won: {approach}: the mayor's rider carries a letter to {ruler} ({roll}). {People} march
ally.lost: {approach}: the mayor's letter reaches {ruler} ({roll}), and changes nothing.
